key_insight: Variational quantum circuits can generate exact uniform permutations on constrained hardware, achieving linear-depth controlled-SWAP constructions on nearest-neighbor layouts.
engineering_relevance: This reduces connectivity demands and depth for uniform permutation sampling, making the method more practical for quantum hardware and compiler-aware circuit design.
method: Build a variational circuit whose gate layout follows the device interaction graph.
Use controlled-SWAP-based unitary constructions to enforce exact uniform permutation statistics.
Analyze topology limits and show Bene61-like architectures can realize permutations but not uniform sampling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact uniformity with quadratic circuit size and linear depth O(n) on linear nearest-neighbor topologies, plus a proof of intrinsic non-uniformity for quantum Bene61-like circuits.
watch_item: Exact uniformity is topology-dependent and may require substantial circuit size and careful parameter optimization, which could affect noise robustness and scalability.
paper_title: Variational Approach for Uniform Quantum Permutation Generators
